sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module overview and imports
sections.what: Nothing runs here. It explains the two kinds of sensitivity test and loads the copy tool.
sections.why: Gives the reader the purpose before the code.

sections.name: sensitivity_1way
sections.title: Testing one input across a range
sections.what: Reruns the model once for each value in a list, changing only one input, and records one output from each run.
sections.why: Shows how a single assumption moves the result.
sections.watch_out: A missing output name silently records an empty value for that run.

sections.name: sensitivity_2way (part 1)
sections.title: Building the two-input grid
sections.what: For each pair of values from the two lists, reruns the model with both inputs set and records the output in a grid, one row per first-variable value.
sections.why: Shows how two assumptions work together.
sections.watch_out: Rows follow the first variable and columns follow the second, so swapping the two lists turns the table sideways.

sections.name: sensitivity_2way (part 2)
sections.title: Returning the grid and labels
sections.what: Returns the grid together with the names and values of both variables.
sections.why: Gives the caller everything needed to label the table.

sections.name: create_wacc_terminal_growth_sensitivity
sections.title: Cost of capital against terminal growth table
sections.what: Sets up the usual table of cost of capital against terminal growth. If no ranges are given, it uses default ranges around the base cost of capital and from 1 to 5 percent growth, and tracks equity value.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is a common table in valuation work.
sections.watch_out: The cost of capital is passed in as a plain input, but the valuation function calculates its own, so this table may not change anything.

sections.name: create_revenue_growth_sensitivity
sections.title: Revenue growth against equity value
sections.what: Sets up a one-way test of equity value across revenue growth rates, by default from minus 5 percent to 10 percent.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows how a sales downturn or boom changes value.
sections.watch_out: Only works if the model function reads a key named revenue_growth; otherwise every value gives the same result.

summary: Tests how a result changes when one or two inputs change, by rerunning the model for each setting and producing tables of results.
purpose: Produces tables showing equity value across ranges of cost of capital, terminal growth, or revenue growth.
why: Shows how sensitive the valuation is to its assumptions, which is important when judging risk.
how: 1. Copy the base inputs. 2. Set the tested variable to one value. 3. Rerun the calculation function. 4. Read the chosen output. 5. Repeat for every value; for two variables, repeat for every combination.
inputs: A dictionary of base inputs; the names and ranges of the variables to test; a function that runs the model and returns a dictionary of results; the name of the output to track.
outputs: For one variable, the tested values and matching outputs. For two variables, a grid of outputs with row and column labels.
risks: Setting a variable does nothing unless the model function reads it. The cost of capital and revenue growth tables depend on keys that this file does not check. A missing output name gives empty values without an error. If the base inputs have no wacc key, a default of 10 percent is used.
debug: If every row of the grid is the same, the model function is probably not reading the changed input. If results are empty, check the output name. Test one value and compare it with the base model result.
